detail.longDescription: I'm building a chatbot feature for a water billing office project. The whole feature runs with Docker Compose: a Postgres + pgvector database, a Java REST API, and DynamoDB Local. Every time a user asks the chatbot something, the API saves the interaction (prompt, response, sources and date) in a DynamoDB table so the administrator can review it later. This is how DynamoDB Local is defined in my docker-compose.yml . I run it in memory because it is only for local development and testing: dynamodb: image: amazon/dynamodb-local ports: - "8000:8000" command: "-jar DynamoDBLocal.jar -sharedDb -inMemory" The containers start without errors, but since the database is in memory, the table does not exist when the environment starts from scratch. Because of that, the API throws a ResourceNotFoundException when it tries to save the first interaction. At the moment I solve it by creating the table manually from my machine with the AWS CLI every time I start the environment: aws dynamodb create-table --table-name ChatbotLogs \ --attribute-definitions AttributeName=id,AttributeType=S \ --key-schema AttributeName=id,KeyType=HASH \ --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST \ --endpoint-url http://localhost:8000 This works, but it is easy to forget, and the other members of my team also have to remember to run it. I want docker compose up to leave everything ready without manual steps. I found two possible approaches, but I'm not sure which one is considered better practice: Adding an extra container (for example amazon/aws-cli ) that runs create-table once DynamoDB Local is up. Creating the table from the Java API at startup, only if it does not already exist. Which approach is recommended, and how can I make sure the table creation waits until DynamoDB Local is actually accepting connections?
